name: Independent internal normal controls
tagline: Optional for future mixed samples; none identified in current homogeneous cell line

steps.title: Select controls before comparing
steps.text: Select independently supported cells with compatible assay, build and regional DNA evidence. A lineage label alone does not establish copy neutrality.

steps.title: Build the reference
steps.text: Aggregate their 100 kb bin counts with a documented library-size normalization, checking callable coverage and variation between donors.

steps.title: Compare and stress-test
steps.text: Compare query counts with the reference and leave donors or cell groups out; uncertainty grows where reference coverage is poor.

example.title: Toy matched-control comparison
example.setup: Suppose 20 independently characterized control cells and 30 query cells have counts in the same bin grid.
steps: Normalize each cell for exposure; aggregate the 20 controls.
A query bin is 0.7 relative to the reference; repeat excluding one donor.
example.interpretation: A stable relative decrease is consistent with a difference, not an absolute copy state.

adaptation.first_experiment: Audit control identity and compare donor-held-out reference profiles.
adaptation.success: Reference profiles remain stable within prespecified uncertainty across held-out controls.

cautions: Independent provenance is needed; shared germline changes and accessibility differ by cell type.
This is exploratory; no normal population or absolute CN anchor is assumed.

name: Compatible external normal reference / Numbat-multiome ATAC-bin
tagline: Candidate only after matching reference and verifying input counts and SNP data Public candidate: Zhang adult tissue sci-ATAC atlas GSE184462; per-sample fragments and barcode-to-label compatibility require audit, and copy neutrality is unproven.

steps.title: Choose a compatible atlas
steps.text: Published Numbat-multiome ATAC-bin workflows use normal-cell reference counts and phased SNP-level observations.

steps.title: Rebuild compatible bins
steps.text: Re-bin genuine scATAC fragments using matching coordinates and counting rules, then normalize reference by cell type; check donors and assay chemistry.

steps.title: Combine evidence
steps.text: The published model combines reference-relative counts and phased allele observations. Check coverage and phase provenance before any comparison.

example.title: Toy external reference
example.setup: A query and two external donors have matched 100 kb bins and genuine fragment counts.
steps: Normalize within donor and make a bin-by-cell-type reference.
Compare query relative depth; repeat while leaving each donor out.
example.interpretation: A changing contrast signals reference mismatch; allele-site observations remain a separate, dependent evidence stream.

adaptation.first_experiment: Audit atlas fragments, build, donor labels and count compatibility.
adaptation.success: Held-out donor differences meet prespecified mismatch tolerances.

cautions: Protocol, cell type, batch, assembly, coverage and control CN mismatch confound reference; source data may require access and license checks.
This is exploratory; no normal population or absolute CN anchor is assumed.

name: Reference-free relative baseline sensitivity
tagline: Directly applicable as exploratory sensitivity after provenance audit

steps.title: Choose relative baselines
steps.text: Use the existing genome-wide centering as one baseline and specify alternative robust regional baselines before looking at candidate calls.

steps.title: Normalize depth
steps.text: Account for cell exposure and compare retained callable bins while recording how each baseline is defined.

steps.title: Measure sensitivity
steps.text: Repeat after excluding candidate regions and across coverage strata. A shared broad event can be absorbed by every self-baseline.

example.title: Toy self-centering
example.setup: A cell has normalized values 8, 9, 10 and 13 in four callable bins.
steps: Center by the mean 10, yielding relative values 0.8, 0.9, 1.0 and 1.3.
Repeat with a prespecified alternate baseline and report changes.
example.interpretation: These are relative contrasts; the center has no established diploid meaning.

adaptation.first_experiment: Compare existing centering with a frozen robust alternative.
adaptation.success: Report sensitivity and abstain where direction changes or coverage is insufficient.

cautions: Shared broad events are absorbed into baseline; whole-genome ploidy unidentifiable; baseline changes can reverse calls.
This is exploratory; no normal population or absolute CN anchor is assumed.

name: Signac / ArchR label transfer
tagline: Optional future candidate discovery, not currently runnable with only 100 kb CN bins

steps.title: Find comparable cells
steps.text: Signac integrates compatible accessibility datasets; ArchR can integrate ATAC gene scores with a labelled RNA reference.

steps.title: Transfer annotations
steps.text: Use reference-query correspondences to transfer candidate cell-type labels and scores; inspect low confidence and out-of-reference cells.

steps.title: Separate identity from CN
steps.text: Use labels only to nominate possible matched groups, then seek independent regional DNA and control evidence.

example.title: Toy label transfer
example.setup: Suppose a compatible reference contains 100 labelled epithelial and 100 immune cells.
steps: Project 50 query cells and obtain labels and transfer scores.
Compare matched groups only after checking coverage and independent control provenance.
example.interpretation: A 0.9 transfer score describes annotation confidence in that workflow; it does not establish normal copy number.

adaptation.first_experiment: Check whether compatible peak or fragment inputs exist.
adaptation.success: Labels replicate known cell identities without being used as CN truth.

cautions: Out-of-reference cells can get misleading labels; prediction scores require calibration; missing peak or gene activity inputs.
This is exploratory; no normal population or absolute CN anchor is assumed.

name: CN-selected controls: CopyscAT / CopyKAT / inferCNV
tagline: Comparator or sensitivity analysis, not validation of normal status

steps.title: Select candidate controls
steps.text: CopyscAT offers inferred or supplied controls; CopyKAT and inferCNV are RNA approaches, not scATAC callers.

steps.title: Center on candidates
steps.text: Form relative profiles against chosen candidate cells, retaining the original selection rule and coverage filters.

steps.title: Test for circularity
steps.text: If the same CN pattern selected and evaluated controls, separation is not independent validation; shared alterations may disappear.

example.title: Toy CN-selected baseline
example.setup: Suppose 40 cells all share a broad alteration but 10 have the lowest apparent variation.
steps: Choose those 10 by a frozen variation rule and center the other cells.
Compare against an independently selected baseline and a held-out chromosome.
example.interpretation: A flat selected group may reflect a shared event, rather than a normal population.

adaptation.first_experiment: Measure sensitivity to control selection without calling selected cells normal.
adaptation.success: Report changes in contrasts and any unresolved shared events.

cautions: Shared alterations can be absorbed; homogeneous altered populations lack identifiable normal group; RNA methods are not ATAC callers.
This is exploratory; no normal population or absolute CN anchor is assumed.

name: DNA panel of normals as technical analogy
tagline: Consider only assay-matched independently characterized scATAC panel

steps.title: Learn recurring artifacts
steps.text: DNA panels aggregate compatible control samples to characterize recurrent technical variation across genomic bins.

steps.title: Denoise relative counts
steps.text: A DNA workflow uses the panel to reduce shared technical patterns before relative CN interpretation.

steps.title: Assess transfer
steps.text: An scATAC analogue would require matched assay and cell-state controls; DNA panels cannot directly represent chromatin accessibility.

example.title: Toy panel analogy
example.setup: Suppose five matched scATAC controls show a recurring technical spike in one 100 kb bin.
steps: Record the spike and compare a sixth held-out control.
Check whether a proposed panel adjustment suppresses it without erasing DNA-supported events.
example.interpretation: This is a proposed scATAC adaptation, not an established panel or copy-neutral anchor.

adaptation.first_experiment: Assess reproducibility of bin-level artifacts in held-out controls.
adaptation.success: Technical effects generalize while prespecified DNA-supported contrasts remain detectable.

cautions: A DNA panel ignores cell-type chromatin accessibility; panel artifacts and donor CNVs can bias calls.
This is exploratory; no normal population or absolute CN anchor is assumed.

name: Atacformer
tagline: Conditional zero-shot comparison once genuine peaks/fragments and confirmed assembly exist. 100 kb count bins do not encode appropriate accessible intervals.

steps.title: Tokenize accessible intervals
steps.text: Atacformer overlaps each cell’s accessible intervals with its fixed hg38 vocabulary, producing a set of region tokens; 100 kb count bins are not peaks.

steps.title: Learn context
steps.text: Region embeddings pass through transformer blocks with multi-head attention. Pretraining identifies randomly replaced tokens using their context.

steps.title: Pool representations
steps.text: Contextual region embeddings can be pooled into a cell embedding for exploratory comparisons; token presence need not preserve dosage.

example.title: Toy interval mapping
example.setup: A cell has three real accessible intervals and a verified hg38 vocabulary.
steps: Overlap intervals with vocabulary regions and encode matched tokens.
Pool contextual embeddings, then compare them with a simple peak-based embedding.
example.interpretation: Nearby points indicate a learned accessibility resemblance, not a CN state.

adaptation.first_experiment: Check vocabulary overlap and compare embeddings on independent benchmark samples.
adaptation.success: Prespecified event discrimination improves without depth or sample confounding.

cautions: Token presence and pooling may discard count dosage; coverage/sequence distribution shift may drive embedding; fine tuning can remove or introduce CN structure.
Checkpoint weight license not stated on inspected model card; verify before reuse.
Accessibility embeddings and predictions are not calibrated CN calls; independent DNA validation is required.

name: PEAKVI
tagline: Conditional baseline for accessibility representation once compatible peak matrix exists, not this pass.

steps.title: Encode accessibility
steps.text: PEAKVI fits a variational autoencoder to peak-by-cell accessibility observations and learns a latent representation for each cell.

steps.title: Model detection
steps.text: It models whether a peak has any observations as Bernoulli with accessibility probability multiplied by cell- and region-specific detection factors.

steps.title: Decode probabilities
steps.text: The decoder estimates peak accessibility probabilities; these are not probabilities of a CN state.

example.title: Toy detection probability
example.setup: For one peak in one cell, suppose accessibility is 0.8 and cell and region factors are 0.5 and 0.75.
steps: Multiply 0.8 × 0.5 × 0.75 to obtain a model detection probability of 0.30.
A zero observation remains plausible even when estimated accessibility is high.
example.interpretation: These hypothetical parameters illustrate the model; they do not imply deletion or verified values.

adaptation.first_experiment: Fit a frozen peak-based comparator on compatible benchmark data.
adaptation.success: Measure held-out performance and depth sensitivity against a simple baseline.

cautions: Binarization loses count magnitude; detection probabilities and latent uncertainty are not CN confidence; training required.
OOD behavior is not established.
Accessibility embeddings and predictions are not calibrated CN calls; independent DNA validation is required.

name: SCALE
tagline: Secondary simple learned representation comparator if compatible peak data appear.

steps.title: Compress peaks
steps.text: SCALE encodes a sparse peak-by-cell matrix into a low-dimensional distribution for each cell using a variational autoencoder.

steps.title: Represent mixtures
steps.text: Its prior uses multiple Gaussian components, encouraging latent structure; the decoder models binary accessibility with Bernoulli probabilities.

steps.title: Use embeddings carefully
steps.text: Clustering or imputation can reveal accessibility patterns, but inferred groups and filled values do not independently establish CN.

example.title: Toy mixture
example.setup: Suppose 200 cells have a compatible matrix of 10,000 peaks.
steps: Train with a fixed seed and specified number of mixture components.
Compare the embedding against simple peak-based features on held-out DNA-labelled samples.
example.interpretation: A separated group may reflect cell state, batch or CN; the mixture component is not a copy state.

adaptation.first_experiment: Evaluate reproducibility across seeds and depth strata.
adaptation.success: Any added signal replicates on held-out samples without excessive depth association.

cautions: Filtering and imputation can alter dosage and amplify circularity; no calibrated CN uncertainty.
Documentation reflects older releases; current maintenance not established.
Accessibility embeddings and predictions are not calibrated CN calls; independent DNA validation is required.

name: ChromFound
tagline: Defer: greater setup cost and no evidence of CN advantage; current bins incompatible.

steps.title: Map to a genome vocabulary
steps.text: ChromFound uses genome-aware tokenization of accessible regions to represent a cell across a standardized region universe.

steps.title: Model local and long context
steps.text: Its hybrid encoder combines windowed attention with Mamba sequence modeling to capture local and longer-range dependencies.

steps.title: Reconstruct masked signals
steps.text: The published objective masks zero and nonzero regions and predicts normalized log-transformed accessibility with mean squared error.

example.title: Toy masked-region task
example.setup: Suppose compatible peak data map to 1,000 vocabulary regions in a cell.
steps: Mask a subset of observed and zero entries according to the model protocol.
Predict masked normalized signals and compare with observed signals on held-out cells.
example.interpretation: Reconstruction measures accessibility prediction, not independent CN validation.

adaptation.first_experiment: Verify input compatibility and checkpoint terms before a held-out comparison.
adaptation.success: A reproducible accessibility diagnostic adds value over a simple baseline without CN leakage.

cautions: Code repository identifies Apache-2.0; model weight terms must be checked separately.
Example metadata requires cell type column; cannot assume labels.
Accessibility embeddings and predictions are not calibrated CN calls; independent DNA validation is required.

name: EpiFoundation
tagline: Defer: input and checkpoint/vocabulary need verification, gene prediction adds no direct CN evidence.

steps.title: Encode peak accessibility
steps.text: EpiFoundation starts with binarized peak accessibility and embeds peak and genomic context for a transformer encoder.

steps.title: Align modalities
steps.text: Pretraining uses paired multiome data to align ATAC-derived representations with gene expression; the published task links peak information to genes.

steps.title: Apply downstream
steps.text: Cell embeddings and gene-expression predictions describe learned regulatory relationships, not direct DNA copy measurements.

example.title: Toy cross-modality
example.setup: Suppose 500 paired cells have matched peaks and RNA counts in a compatible vocabulary.
steps: Encode each cell’s observed peak set.
Predict a gene expression profile and compare with RNA held out from training.
example.interpretation: Accurate predicted expression does not independently confirm a CN event affecting that gene.

adaptation.first_experiment: Verify checkpoint, features and peak-to-gene preprocessing on benchmark data.
adaptation.success: Held-out performance is reproducible and independent CN evaluation remains separate.

cautions: Binarized peaks remove read magnitude; paired RNA setup and downstream decoders complicate transfer.
Code and weights license not verified.
Accessibility embeddings and predictions are not calibrated CN calls; independent DNA validation is required.

name: scBasset
tagline: Defer: peak/FASTA inputs, fitting cost and binary objective mismatch CN task.

steps.title: Read DNA sequence
steps.text: scBasset converts peak sequences from a matched reference FASTA into one-hot nucleotide inputs for a convolutional neural network.

steps.title: Learn region and cell features
steps.text: The network learns sequence-derived region embeddings jointly with cell embeddings to reconstruct a binary peak-by-cell accessibility matrix.

steps.title: Predict accessibility
steps.text: The learned model predicts accessibility from sequence and cell features; the training objective does not directly infer dosage.

example.title: Toy sequence model
example.setup: A dataset has 1,000 peak sequences and 200 cells with binary peak calls.
steps: Train using the aligned sequences and matrix with a recorded seed.
Predict held-out peak accessibility and assess performance by cell and depth.
example.interpretation: A predicted accessible peak is a regulatory prediction, not new independent evidence of copy number.

adaptation.first_experiment: Audit genuine peak inputs before considering a trained benchmark.
adaptation.success: Predictions generalize to held-out cells and do not substitute for DNA validation.

cautions: Sequence and cellular accessibility are confounded with dosage; imputed values cannot validate unobserved CN.
Accessibility embeddings and predictions are not calibrated CN calls; independent DNA validation is required.

name: Sample-specific phased heterozygous SNP availability
tagline: Highest priority; per-site auxiliary tables may support ascertainment audit

steps.title: Identify selected variants
steps.text: Inspect the sample genotype and phase inputs; the audited builder selects phased 0|1 or 1|0 calls and exact chromosome, position, REF and ALT matches.

steps.title: Map and aggregate
steps.text: Convert coordinates carefully and sum selected SNP-site depth within each bin and cell. AT is a sum of site observations, not necessarily unique fragments.

steps.title: Track missingness
steps.text: Record candidate, selected and observed SNP counts separately. Phase-set continuity and historical execution remain unverified.

example.title: Toy site audit
example.setup: A 100 kb bin contains five candidate SNPs, two selected heterozygotes and site depths 3 and 4.
steps: Match both alleles exactly and map the sites to the bin.
Sum the selected site depths to AT = 7; retain the number of selected sites.
example.interpretation: AT = 7 is not seven unique molecules, and AT = 0 does not indicate balanced alleles.

adaptation.first_experiment: Audit selection and counting units in fixed bins.
adaptation.success: Reconcile site counts with AT while explicitly retaining unresolved phase.

cautions: Observed het density is not population reference density; phase labels absent from matrices; filter-induced selection and LOH can reduce sites
Counting unit and run parameters unknown
This is exploratory; no normal population or absolute CN anchor is assumed.

name: ENCODE blacklist and genomic gap mask
tagline: High; check historical blacklist before any new exclusions

steps.title: Match coordinates
steps.text: Obtain assembly-matched blacklist and assembly gap intervals and confirm BED coordinate conventions.

steps.title: Calculate overlap
steps.text: For each original 100 kb bin, compute the fraction overlapping blacklisted intervals and flag gap intersections.

steps.title: Keep exclusions visible
steps.text: Compare retained and original grids and test flagged versus unflagged sensitivity without inventing reasons for missing historical bins.

example.title: Toy interval overlap
example.setup: A 100 kb bin overlaps 20 kb of blacklist and 5 kb of assembly gap.
steps: Calculate blacklist overlap as 20% and mark the gap.
Compare results with and without the flagged bin as a prespecified sensitivity analysis.
example.interpretation: The annotation flags technical uncertainty; it does not establish deletion or explain a missing bin.

adaptation.first_experiment: Annotate overlaps without imposing a new default mask.
adaptation.success: Coordinates reconcile and interpretations report sensitivity to flags.

cautions: Low accessibility is not synonymous with blacklist; whole-bin exclusion can remove genuine events
Cannot infer why individual missing bins were removed from retained grid alone
This is exploratory; no normal population or absolute CN anchor is assumed.

name: Umap multi-read mappability
tagline: Useful later once read parameters and track license confirmed

steps.title: Choose a matching track
steps.text: Select a multi-read mappability track for the confirmed assembly, contigs and relevant read length.

steps.title: Summarize per bin
steps.text: Intersect the track with each 100 kb bin and summarize the fraction or continuous score; record missing track coverage.

steps.title: Use as a sensitivity flag
steps.text: A low value signals possible mapping ambiguity, not an observed sample-specific mapping rate or a copy state.

example.title: Toy mappability annotation
example.setup: Suppose a compatible track indicates 60 kb of a 100 kb bin has a score of 1 and 40 kb a score of 0.
steps: Compute the mean track score as 0.60.
Compare depth interpretation for high- and low-scoring bins without automatically excluding either.
example.interpretation: This simplified calculation describes reference uniqueness; real tracks and paired-end behavior need verification.

adaptation.first_experiment: Join track summaries to bins after checking provenance.
adaptation.success: Sensitivity estimates remain interpretable across mappability strata.

cautions: Single-read and multi-read scores differ; paired-end mapping and genetic variation alter applicability
No threshold validated for CNV inference
This is exploratory; no normal population or absolute CN anchor is assumed.

sources.title: Umap and Bismap: quantifying genome and methylome mappability

name: GC content and existing correction
tagline: GC exists in retained-grid var, usable without external join after provenance check

steps.title: Calculate GC
steps.text: Use a confirmed reference FASTA to calculate the fraction of G and C bases in each retained bin; existing GC values require provenance checks.

steps.title: Inspect correction
steps.text: Published epiAneufinder uses per-cell LOESS GC correction; determine whether and how the historical run applied it.

steps.title: Compare signals
steps.text: Compare raw depth, GC and processed values across callable bins without treating corrected values as new observations.

example.title: Toy GC check
example.setup: Two 100 kb bins have GC fractions 0.35 and 0.65 and raw counts 10 and 5 in one cell.
steps: Plot counts against GC across many bins and inspect the fitted trend.
Compare the candidate contrast before and after the existing documented correction.
example.interpretation: A changed contrast may reflect bias correction or attenuation of biological signal; neither is established by this example.

adaptation.first_experiment: Audit raw and processed depth against GC using existing code.
adaptation.success: Report event sensitivity and preserve raw observations.

cautions: GC correlates with technical and biological signals; correction can attenuate events
Actual reference and configuration need audit
This is exploratory; no normal population or absolute CN anchor is assumed.

name: Cell-type accessibility prior
tagline: Defer until peak or fragment data and sample matching are established

steps.title: Find relevant context
steps.text: Choose a tissue- and state-matched accessibility atlas with compatible assay, assembly, peaks and cell labels.

steps.title: Summarize accessibility
steps.text: Aggregate genuine peak or fragment observations by independently annotated cell type and compare corresponding genomic regions.

steps.title: Treat as context
steps.text: A region with low accessibility in a reference cell state may be difficult to observe; it is not automatically deleted in a query.

example.title: Toy context comparison
example.setup: In a compatible atlas, 5 of 100 matched cells have a peak detected in one region.
steps: Record the 5% detection frequency alongside query depth.
Repeat with another donor and compatible cell state.
example.interpretation: Low reference detection is contextual evidence for sparse observation, not copy-neutral or deletion truth.

adaptation.first_experiment: First assess whether compatible peak inputs and tissue context exist.
adaptation.success: Context is reproducible across donors and kept separate from CN validation.

cautions: Cell-type mismatch and CN confounding; circularity if same focal evidence defines prior
This is exploratory; no normal population or absolute CN anchor is assumed.
